findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, exposing the MySQL endpoint to the internet. Combined with the "admin" username and a password sourced from var.password, this presents an internet-reachable authentication surface.
storage_encrypted = false means the MySQL database, its backups, and snapshots are stored unencrypted, so anyone with access to the underlying storage or snapshots can read the data.

The database endpoint, admin username, and the literal password var.password are interpolated into the EC2 instance's user_data and written to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. user_data is readable via instance metadata (IMDS) and the file is world-readable on the host, so the credential is disclosed to anyone who can reach the instance or its metadata service.

The MySQL ingress rule allows 0.0.0.0/0 to reach port 3306 on the database security group, so the entire internet can attempt to connect to the database. Ingress should be restricted to the application security group only.

The database security group has no restrictive egress defined and the only egress rule is fully open (catalog_db_outbound), allowing the database to initiate outbound connections to any destination, which facilitates data exfiltration if the instance is compromised.
Egress rule permits protocol -1 (all) to 0.0.0.0/0, giving the database unrestricted outbound network access, which enables data exfiltration and outbound C2 traffic.

The policy grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*", giving the application role full control over all S3 buckets, EC2 instances, and RDS databases in the account. Any compromise of the app server yields broad control-plane access.

The instance user_data embeds the database password (var.password) and admin username directly in the launch script, exposing secrets through instance metadata and the rendered /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc file.
The database is created with a fixed privileged username "admin", increasing the impact of any credential exposure and simplifying brute-force targeting of the account.

skip_final_snapshot = true combined with backup_retention_period = 0 means the database is destroyed with no retained data, which is a data-availability concern rather than a security vulnerability; noted here only for completeness.
